# Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans — concept pack (small)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Conftest recognizes deny, violation, and warn rules, including identifier suffixes such as deny_myrule. Its documentation shows Rego v1-style deny contains msg if syntax and conftest verify --policy ./policy for executing policy unit tests. (low confidence) — https://www.conftest.dev/

## How it works

- [statement] planned_values omits values that are still unknown. It describes the known planned outcome; resource_changes separately records the operations that lead to it. (low confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format
- [statement] Conftest searches the main namespace by default; --namespace selects a namespace and --all-namespaces evaluates across namespaces. Policies live in policy by default, with --policy overriding that directory. A custom OPA package must be selected explicitly when it is outside main. (high confidence) — https://www.conftest.dev/ · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://www.runatlantis.io/docs/policy-checking.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Plan-time values can be incomplete. planned_values omits unknown values, while change.after_unknown marks unknown leaves with true. Policy authors must confirm required evidence exists and explicitly handle unknowns; a clean result alone cannot prove compliance for attributes known only after apply. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform
- [statement] Inference for Atlas automation: this approach can gate Terraform-managed configuration before deployment only where the relevant provider attributes appear in plan JSON. It cannot by itself verify live query-log collection, actual Performance Advisor results, or settings and mutations outside the inspected plan. (medium confidence) — https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Replacement operations have action arrays ["delete", "create"] or ["create", "delete"]. A deletion guard should test membership of "delete" in change.actions rather than equality with ["delete"], which would miss replacements. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform
- [statement] Terraform documents backward-compatible minor changes and incompatible major changes in format_version. Consumers should ignore unknown properties for supported minor versions and reject unsupported major versions rather than silently evaluating a different input contract. (low confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Generate a saved plan with terraform plan -out=tfplan, render it with terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json, and run conftest test tfplan.json --policy policy/ to evaluate Rego policies before apply. OPA documents the saved-plan conversion, while a practitioner demonstrates the Conftest invocation. (high confidence) — https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show, https://rodrigtech.com/conftest-and-authoring-custom-checks-in-policy-as-code/, https://www.conftest.dev/
- [statement] Conftest uses the OPA Rego language to evaluate assertions against structured configuration data, including Terraform inputs. (high confidence) — https://www.conftest.dev/ · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://github.com/open-policy-agent/conftest
- [statement] Plan JSON exposes resource_changes entries with resource type and change.actions; change.before and change.after describe old and proposed values. This supports policies scoped to resource types and operations. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform
- [statement] Conftest discovers deny, violation and warn rules and defaults to the main namespace. Use --namespace for another package or --all-namespaces to evaluate every namespace. A policy in an unselected namespace needs explicit selection. (low confidence) — https://www.conftest.dev/
- [statement] terraform show -json displays sensitive state values in plaintext. Sensitivity metadata such as after_sensitive identifies sensitive leaves for consumers; it does not by itself remove the underlying values. Protect plan JSON and redact displayed policy diagnostics. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format
- [statement] Atlantis documents server-side Conftest checks on plan output. Its documented apply blocking requires policy checking together with the mergeable apply requirement, and policy owners can approve failures. Thus enforcement depends on workflow and approval configuration. (low confidence) — https://www.runatlantis.io/docs/policy-checking.html
- [statement] Conftest can unit-test policies with conftest verify --policy ./policy. Rego tests can substitute input and data with the with keyword. The documentation demonstrates passing and failing configuration tests. (low confidence) — https://www.conftest.dev/
- [statement] A saved-plan JSON export includes the plan, configuration, and prior state. Omitting the file argument from terraform show -json instead exports the latest state snapshot, so a plan gate must explicitly pass the saved plan. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format
- [statement] Plan policies can iterate input.resource_changes, select resources by type or address, and inspect change.actions and change.after to evaluate prospective operations and attributes. (high confidence) — https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format, https://www.runatlantis.io/docs/policy-checking.html
- [statement] Terraform plan -json emits machine-readable UI messages, including planned_change events that omit the detailed attribute changes. It is a different interface from terraform show -json <saved-plan>; do not substitute the UI event stream for the saved-plan document expected by resource_changes policies. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/machine-readable-ui · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format, https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show
- [statement] terraform show -json can expose sensitive state values in plaintext; plan JSON includes prior state and attribute sensitivity metadata. Treat saved JSON as sensitive and avoid publishing raw plan artifacts or logging their full contents. (high confidence) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show · keywords: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format
